clue.text: Job in Rome gets money without limit when returned

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the money word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: pay is money earned

indicators.note: returned means the word for a limit is read backwards before it goes in

parts.note: a cap is an upper limit, as on spending

explanation.surface: Someone with a job in Rome is getting unlimited money paid back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking; 'when returned' reverses only the limit word, which sits inside the money word.
explanation.definitionFit: The office held by the Pope, whose seat is in Rome, is a post or job.

clue.text: H's friend has little time between rounds

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: between means the time piece sits between the two round letters

parts.note: a round shape looks like the letter O
a second round shape gives another O
min is the short form of minute, a little time

explanation.surface: A heroin user's friend has little time between rounds of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: Throughout this puzzle H stands for a horse, the theme; 'rounds' gives two Os, with MIN between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A palomino is a horse with a golden coat and pale mane, one of the theme's breeds and types.

clue.text: Rope trick shares rhetorical conclusions

indicators.note: a trick plays on things, so the letters of rope are rearranged

parts.note: rations are allotted shares

explanation.surface: A rope trick divides things up and so wraps up a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trick' is the anagram signal on the first word; 'shares' looks like a verb but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A peroration is the closing part of a speech, summing it up with rhetorical force.

clue.text: H for shooter

definitions.meaning: in this puzzle H stands for horse: a young male one

explanation.definitionFit: A colt is a young male horse, and Colt is the maker of a famous revolver or shooter.

clue.text: One like this drinks things that may be radioactive

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
so means in this way, like this
to tope is an old word for to drink heavily

explanation.surface: Someone like this takes drink after drink of radioactive things.
explanation.definitionFit: Variants of an element with different neutron counts; some are unstable and give off radiation.

clue.text: Quiet time kept by antelope in islands with H

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: kept by means the time letter is held inside the antelope

parts.note: an eland is a large African antelope

explanation.surface: A quiet moment kept by an antelope on islands with heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kept by' is the container signal. The Shetland Islands, north of Scotland, give their name to a small hardy pony, hence 'with H'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Shetland Islands lie north of Scotland and are home to the small, hardy pony named after them.

clue.text: Water with boats moving in pairs

indicators.note: moving suggests things being shifted around, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Boats on the water moving side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking or going side by side, two at a time, is going in pairs.

clue.text: See 28
Mountaineer or show jumper, a legend in the home counties

indicators.note: in means the legend is placed inside the region letters

parts.note: SE, the south-east of England, holds the home counties around London
a myth is a legend

explanation.surface: A climber or show jumper is a legend around the counties near London.
explanation.walkthrough: The home counties are those around London, in the south-east (SE) of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Smythe was a noted mountaineer and Pat Smythe a famous show jumper, both bearing this surname.

clue.text: H given drink takes nothing

parts.note: a pint is a drink, typically of beer
nought, written as O, is nothing

explanation.surface: Given a drink, the heroin user takes nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinto is a piebald or spotted horse, popular in the American West.

clue.text: Hardy fellow and I heard a siren

indicators.note: heard means the words are sounded out, so we want a name that is pronounced the same

parts.note: Stan Laurel was Oliver Hardy's comedy partner, followed by I

explanation.surface: Hardy's partner and I both heard a siren call.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel and Hardy were a film comedy duo; LAUREL said with I sounds like the siren's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the Rhine siren of legend who lured boatmen to the rocks with her singing.

clue.text: English H with setter's way of naming places for people

definitions.text: way of naming places for people

parts.note: in this puzzle H stands for a horse, here a small one
the setter's is my, from the setter's point of view

explanation.surface: An English horse joins the setter in a way of naming places after people.
explanation.definitionFit: Naming something, a place for instance, after a person is the practice called by this term.

clue.text: Sea H?

definitions.meaning: Latin for sea, used for the dark plains on the Moon
in this puzzle H is a horse: a female one

explanation.definitionFit: Latin and lunar maps use this word for a sea, and it is also a female horse.

clue.text: Bad result for Labour?

parts.note: labour as childbirth, not the political party: its sad outcome when the baby is dead

explanation.definitionFit: When labour in childbirth ends with the baby born dead, that is the sad result.

clue.text: Custom of being on H in Yorkshire dress?

parts.note: Yorkshire was divided into three Ridings
a habit is a form of dress, as a nun's

explanation.surface: A custom of riding horses in Yorkshire dress.
explanation.walkthrough: Yorkshire was historically split into three Ridings (North, East and West); the first definition reads as a habit of riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing worn for horse-riding, read jokingly as the habit or custom of riding.

clue.text: H with dyes called "Transformation"

indicators.note: a transformation changes the form of these two words, rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A heroin dealer with hair dyes named Transformation.
explanation.definitionFit: A Clydesdale is a large Scottish draught horse, named after the Clyde valley.

clue.text: Catcher let off with sting?

parts.note: a net catches things

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A goalkeeper let one in and is stung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is the anagram signal on 'let'; the question mark flags that 'sting' is a verb meaning to irritate.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate or provoke someone is to sting them, as the stinging plant does.

clue.text: Disobedient in a scout and ill-advised in a king

definitions.meaning: a scout disobeys the motto Be Prepared if not prepared
the epithet of King Ethelred of England, from an Old English word for poor counsel

explanation.definitionFit: Not prepared breaks the scouts' motto, and Ethelred's epithet originally meant poorly counselled.

clue.text: Sweetmeat injurious to high class regimen

indicators.note: something injurious damages things, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: U is upper class, the posh usage

explanation.surface: A sweet that does harm to a top-drawer diet.
explanation.walkthrough: U (upper class) and REGIMEN are rearranged by 'injurious to'.
explanation.definitionFit: This light baked confection of whipped egg white and sugar is a sweet dish.

clue.text: Space with traditional elevation in place of H

indicators.note: in a down answer an elevation lifts the pieces up, reading them backwards

parts.note: room is space
trad is short for traditional, as in trad jazz

explanation.surface: Room with a traditional elevation in place of heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'elevation' reverses everything: ROOM + TRAD read upwards. Dartmoor is a moorland in Devon with wild ponies.
explanation.definitionFit: Dartmoor in Devon is the home of a native breed of pony that roams wild there.

clue.text: Join together around one serviceman

indicators.note: around means the joining word goes round the single letter

parts.note: to solder is to join metal together
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Join together around one serviceman.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an army is a serviceman.

clue.text: African second in friendly islands

indicators.note: in means the second's letter goes inside the islands

parts.note: Tonga is known as the Friendly Islands

explanation.surface: An African second in the Friendly Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Cook named Tonga the Friendly Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tsonga are a people of southern Africa, in Mozambique and South Africa.

clue.text: H born with stone round roof of mouth

indicators.note: round means the gem goes round the letter taken from the mouth

parts.note: a ruby is a precious stone

indicators.note: in a down answer the roof is the top, the first letter

explanation.surface: A newborn with a stone round the roof of the mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roof of mouth' is the top letter of 'mouth', M, which RUBY goes 'round'.
explanation.definitionFit: A brumby is a wild or feral horse of Australia.

clue.text: Uncommon H, born with defect?

parts.note: a lack is a deficiency or defect

explanation.surface: A rare heroin addict, born with a defect?
explanation.definitionFit: A pure black coat is unusual among horses, so a black one is an uncommon sort.

clue.text: Not too attractive, arousing bit less ire

indicators.note: arousing stirs things up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Not too attractive, stirring a bit less anger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arousing' rearranges BIT, LESS and IRE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be resisted, so not so very attractive or tempting.

clue.text: A little bit of Sunday?

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, as in not a jot
the Sunday of Pentecost, seventh after Easter

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a very small amount and names the feast of Pentecost Sunday.

clue.text: Left wing movement of H

definitions.meaning: a Trotskyist, someone on the far left
H is a horse here: its gait between walk and canter

explanation.definitionFit: A slang name for a Trotskyist on the far left, and a horse's two-beat gait.

clue.text: H has to be suspended, having dropped it

parts.note: must means has to

indicators.note: having dropped means a letter is taken out of the hanging word

parts.note: to hang is to be suspended
it refers back to the H at the start of the clue

explanation.surface: Heroin has to be hung up, having been dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' refers to H, which is dropped from HANG.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a free-roaming horse of the American West.

clue.text: Just card to fold

parts.note: a SIM card goes in a mobile phone
a ply is a layer or fold

explanation.surface: Just a card to fold.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning merely or only, as in it was just a joke.

clue.text: H in company with a buffalo

indicators.note: in means the horse and the letter a go inside the company

parts.note: in this puzzle H is a horse: an Arab is a breed

explanation.surface: A horse in company with a buffalo.
explanation.walkthrough: Here H is not the definition but a piece: ARAB, a horse breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The carabao is the water buffalo of the Philippines.

clue.text: Complained of flower girl turning to only daughter

indicators.note: turning means the girl's name is read backwards

parts.note: May is a girl's name and also the hawthorn's flower
mere means only, as in a mere child

explanation.surface: A flower girl complained of turning into an only daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on at length in a whining way is to grumble or carp.

clue.text: One saying something to old Greek coin

definitions.meaning: a gold or silver coin of ancient Greece

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both one who states and the name of an ancient Greek coin.
